source_title: In the 1860s, Auckland’s Edinburgh castle pub opened on Symonds Street; here’s how ‘Crowded House’ frontman Neil Finn plans to turn the historic venue into wellness retreat

The purchase sits just around the corner from Roundhead, his recording studio, and continues a quiet pattern of acquiring buildings in the neighbourhood he has called home for years.Neil Finnâs pub has a long and difficult pastThe Edinburgh Castle dates back to the 1860s and is one of the few remaining hotels from that era near the top of Symonds Street. Even in its early days it faced pushback. According to the Spinoff in 1865, around 60 residents objected to its liquor licence, arguing the area did not need another hotel. The licence was granted anyway. More than a century later the same concerns returned. Residents and police opposed the renewal of its liquor licence, and the pub surrendered it in 2023. It continued operating for a time as a hotel and gambling venue with poker machines, but that licence ended on 30 November 2025. Finn has been buying properties on the block since at least 2003. Roundhead, his recording studio on Newton Road, has operated in the area for more than twenty years and has hosted artists including Kanye West, Johnny Marr, and KT Tunstall, as well as Crowded House and his son Liam Finn. In the same month he bought the pub, he also paid NZ$1.8 million for a neighbouring former panel-beating workshop on Randolph Street measuring 440 square metres.
